text: Kingsmoor FC triggered their wide attack through a patient, possession-based build-up, completing 11 short passes over 56.5 seconds starting from a throw-in deep in their own half (x=93.5). Central to this was lateral and backward circulation between Hamza Strand and Rafael Sato, which served as a rest-defense mechanism to draw Westport Albion’s direct pressing out of shape and reduce their PPDA pressure to 7.3. The pressing trigger came from field tilt control, as Kingsmoor held 52.4% possession and maintained high pass accuracy (85.9%) to manipulate space. Viktor Quinlan’s progressive long pass into the final third broke the defensive lines, creating an overload on the flank that released Felix Duarte into a high-xG (0.827) open-play shot opportunity inside the box. This sequence highlights Kingsmoor’s strategic use of sustained build-up and progressive passes to generate quality chances in contrast to Westport’s vertical direct style. [#695] [#713] [#713]
